newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B share index ends down sharply.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B share index ends down sharply.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index ended down sharply on Friday on profit-taking following Thursday's rebound, brokers said.
The index fell 3.67 percent or 5.42 points to 142.17 points on volume of 31.25 million shares worth HK$160.6 million against Thursday's HK$168 million.
Brokers said B shares dropped in line with the city's A share market on Friday in the absence of positive news.
The A share index slumped 8.60 points or 2.46 percent to end at 340.42, with turnover rising to 5.92 billion yuan from 5.80 billion yuan in the previous session.

Brokers said the declines in the A and B share markets on Friday were also due in part to rumours that China's patriarch leader Deng Xiaoping was in fragile health and that Beijing planned to launch a new crackdown on illicit stock trading.
"Investors reduced their positions to see whether there would be any negative news on the weekend," one broker said.
(Reuters does not report rumours but covers reasons for significant market price changes.)
All 43 Shenzhen-listed B shares were traded, with 42 falling and one holding steady.
Great Ocean was the worst B share performer, falling HK$0.28 or 6.78 percent to HK$3.85, on trade of 1.02 million shares due in part to profit-taking, brokers said.

Conglomerate Zhonghao slipped HK$0.27 or 6.32 percent to HK$4.00 as 167,400 shares changed hands. Guangdong Power, the most active counter, fell HK$0.11 to HK$7.10 on volume of 3.52 million shares on institutional selling.
Changan Automobile followed suit, skidding HK$0.24 to HK$4.45 on trade of 2.65 million shares.
Automobile parts maker Weifu finished unchanged at HK$4.32, with 419,100 shares traded.
On the A share market, selling targeted a range of recently-listed issues that had accumulated heavy gains over the past few sessions, brokers said.
Tongcheng Group plunged 0.96 yuan or 8.01 percent to 11.03 yuan due to profit-taking, brokers said. Jinwei Textile tumbled 0.94 yuan or 7.65 percent to 11.34 yuan.
